name: The Breach
caption: A level-5 combat one-shot on Chuni's Wall, for four players — by Connor Brashar, converted to Sacadia's Art of War v1.2.
description:
Chuni's Wall is a pale and desolate place. Your station here is an isolated and cold one, as you watch northward into the Upper Heibrim. Demons prowl the lands north of here. You have seen them in the night. They wander aimlessly, forever hungering for the flesh of humanity — hungry for you. It is a quiet and tense post. Until it isn't.

Contents: the Chuni's Wall battle map with tokens, siege engines and an automated pit trap; four pregenerated level-5 Tianqi wall guards; Wanabbul the Vast and three optional demons; a GM guide and player handouts; and the Tianqi culture's cultural abilities and inheritance for players who bring their own characters.

background.appearance: Pale grey-blue eyes and hair, pale off-white skin. White trousers and a white shirt; never wears a cloak, even on the wall.
background.connections: Newer among the wall guards. From Tian Chun, a religious capital of the Tianqi. Mans the great ballista atop the wall.
background.beliefs: The demons of Qianpo can be beaten one punch at a time.
background.secrets: Born of the union of a human and a Sylnid of the lake mists — the mist still clings to him on cold mornings.
background.culturalTies: Tian Chun's temples and their tales of the Ascendant heroes.

system.biography:
Thug, level 5 — Fixerfolk (Sylnfolk of the Mist). Selthimor hits harder every time he hits in a row: get next to the enemy and keep swinging. See the How to Play pages of the player handout.

Binding Laws and Customs (Tianqi)

  • The Rootbinding: support the war against Ager and the demons of Qianpo above law, religion and family.
  • Ascendancy: unless of Noble blood, follow the orders of those with the blood of Ascendant heroes.
  • The Dead: burn the dead immediately and bury their ashes.
  • Right to Victory: whoever deals the final blow claims the spoils, honors and punishment.
  • Touching Gold: unless of Noble blood, never willingly touch or carry gold.

system.description: Your unarmed weapons do 1D6 damage instead of 1D4 base damage dice.

Once per turn, choose one target within 5ft of you. Attempt to give them Wrestle Pin equal to half your Proficiency (rounded up). Finesse Check negates. For as long as they retain levels of Pin, you cannot use one arm.

For every successful melee attack you have made consecutively on your turn against a single target, add 1D4 to damage dealt on additional attacks made (to a total maximum added damage of XD4, where X is your Proficiency).

For every successful melee attack you have made consecutively on your turn against a single target, increase your to-hit on subsequent attacks by +1 (to a max of your Proficiency). The first time you would miss your attack or at the end of your turn, this effect ends.
When you have a target surrounded, you may use a boost to gain 1X Advantage on the first melee attack made against them each turn.
Once per turn when you miss with a melee attack, you may expend one additional AP to re-roll that roll.
Your base damage when you make a melee attack is increased by half your Finesse (rounded up).
You may make a melee attack against an enemy by bashing them with your skull. If you hit, lose X HP and deal XD4+Power damage, where X is equal to your Proficiency.
You do not take damage when you use Pained Bash.
If you successfully hit a single target with four or more melee attacks in a turn, Consecutive Threat applies to Pained Bash.
When you have given a target levels of Wrestle Pin and they only have one level of Pin, increase the damage dice you deal through melee attacks by one dice type.
Gain 1X Advantage on opportunity attacks of any kind. When you attempt to Kick a target, they roll their Trait Check against being moved at 1X Disadvantage.
Your first reaction each turn is always treated as Steadied.
You may use this on any action before or after rolling. If you do, expend one lore point. You critically succeed at that action.
Gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls made with unarmed weapons vs. PD. Additionally, do not reduce your AP on the first turn of combat when you are ambushed.
Prerequisite: Medium Armor Training, Prof[3]

Date (Healing) (Action): Expend one Healing Date from a RIS and choose one target within 5ft (you can choose yourself). Remove one level of Battle Fatigue from that target. A target may benefit from a Healing Date no more than once per quick rest. (First Aid, rulebook p.203.)

Torch (Passive, Action): When you hold a lit torch in one hand it gives off 10ft of bright light and 20ft of dim. In combat you may treat it as a club (5ft melee, 1D6 Bludgeon vs. PD; Fire damage while lit). If you critically fail to hit with it, it goes out. It burns out after one hour, or with a quick rest. (Rulebook p.200.)

On Chuni's Wall: touch or throw a lit torch onto a creature soaked by an Oil Barrel to ignite it — use the Oil Barrel's Ignite ability for the 6D10 Fire damage.

Starting Cultural Talent. You gain 1 level of Talent Specialization in Religion: Demon Lore. This level does not require the Religion General Talent to use, and it stacks with any other levels you would take by leveling into Religion: Demon Lore. Your demon lore also works for all Qianpo demons, even though they are not demons. (Recorded on the Talents tab as Religion: Demon Lore.)

system.description: As a reaction to an ally making an attack roll within 15ft of you, you may add your Courage score to that to-hit. If you have Steadied, also add half your Power (rounded up).

(Add a 'Call Points' entry to your Pools tracker with Max = Proficiency.)

Expend 1 Call Point and make trait checks against one level of any adversarial condition from up to X targets within 15ft of you (X is half your Proficiency, rounded up). The condition can differ for each target.

Expend one call point and choose one ally within 15ft of you, as well as a number of unspent AP up to half your maximum AP (rounded up). Expend those AP now. On your chosen ally's next turn, they receive additional AP equal to the number you expended.
The number of calls you get per quick rest is equal to twice your Proficiency Score, rather than your Proficiency Score.

system.biography:
Level 9 Demon · Gigantic (5×5) · Prof. +5 · 3 AP (plus a 20ft move each turn) · Talents: Perception +13, Athletics +13.

A gigantic, demonic figure who looms up to the height of the top of the wall — a shadowy shape trailing whisps of black smoke. Illuminated in a flash of fire, he appears almost hollow.

Behavior. Wanabbul moves forward 20ft every round, through any obstacle. When he reaches the wall he destroys it in a single turn, then tries to Grab one nearby character. Once he is reduced to half health he sprouts more arms on his next turn and uses Draining Aura. Optional: speed him up to 25ft or 30ft below half health for a faster, slightly easier fight.

Death. A humanoid skeleton — the last remnant of his once-human form — falls to the ground while the rest of him dissipates into mist.

system.description: +12 to-hit against PD. Deal 2D10+5 Piercing on a hit. 5ft range.
+12 to-hit against PD. Deal 2D6+5 Bludgeoning on a hit. 15ft range.
All creatures within 30ft of you on the ground beneath you make a Power Check or are knocked Prone.

Once in combat as you are near the wall, choose one target within 20ft of you. Attempt to give that target 3 levels of Pin (Finesse Check negates). If they take at least one level of Pin, move them to you. They are held in your hand.

If they lose all Pin while in your hand, they may choose to cling to you (make a DC15 Finesse Check to do so) or drop to the ground below (taking 6D6 damage from the fall).

As a Boost to an action while you are holding a creature, you may drop that creature. They may use a reaction to make a DC15 Finesse Check to cling to you, or they fall to the ground, taking 6D6 damage from the fall.
Once per combat, every creature within 30ft of you makes Power Checks against 2 levels of Fatigue. Only use this when you have less than half health.
When you have less than half HP, you sprout additional arms on your body. Do not exhaust each one-arm limb the first time you would use them in combat.

As a gigantic creature, you have 3X advantage against any physical condition (e.g., Pin, Prone) — the v1.2 size rule, applied automatically against Medium creatures.

Creatures may climb onto and stand on this creature. If they do, all movement on it is difficult terrain, and they must make a Power Check to climb (following the Climb Rules), treating it as a slow-moving creature (1X disadvantage).
Wanabbul moves forward 20ft per round through any obstacle. When he reaches Chuni's Wall, he destroys it in a single turn, leaving a wide hole that stops anyone crossing east–west along the wall top.
Rolls Power Checks with 3X Advantage.
Natural armor: 3 points of this creature's PD can be rended (the stat block's "(3)").

system.biography:
Level 9 Demon · Huge (3×3) · Prof. +5 · 4 AP · Talents: Perception +8, Athletics +13.

A writhing, pustulous worm creature. Not as physically intimidating as Wanabbul, but faster: a 20ft move plus Slam's 15ft carries him 35ft a turn.

Behavior. Above half health he won't move past the characters — anyone who stands in front of him gets his attention. Below half HP he races for the southern edge of the map.

The wall. Grubnut can't breach the wall at once: on his first turn attacking it, it splinters; on the second it shatters; on the third he moves through.

Death. He melts, leaving a strong stench, a sizzling corpse of boils and green ooze, and the outline of a dangerously warped human skeleton.

A pustule bursts out this creature's side. Choose one target within 10ft of this creature to make a Courage Check against 4 levels of either Delirium or Nausea.

The same Pustule action as Pustule (Bile) — pick one per use.

Once in combat, all creatures within 60ft of you must make Courage Checks against 6 levels of Nausea.

Move 15ft forward. All creatures in the 15×15 square you move into make a 1X disadvantaged Finesse Check against this creature's Check DC or take 3D10 damage. Can use at most once per turn.

If you slam a wall, the wall takes 5D10 damage and all creatures within 30ft of the point of impact along the wall make a Finesse Check against your Check DC or are knocked Prone. (Apply the 1X disadvantage from the save card.)

This creature is immune to Fatigue and Prone. It has 1X advantage against any physical condition (e.g., Pin) — in v1.2 its Huge size already gives it 2X against Medium creatures, which applies instead.
Rolls Power Checks with 1X Advantage.

system.biography:
Level 9 Demon · Huge (4×4) · Prof. +5 · 5 AP · Move 20ft, Climb 20ft · Talents: Perception +10, Acrobatics +10.

A giant writhing mass of black worms, loosely organized around a human skull somewhere deep within. It keeps a semblance of collective intelligence, but it is alien now.

Behavior. It moves forward each turn; once split, only one mass presses forward while the others hunt characters to slow the party. At the wall it splits in two: one part breaks the wall down over two turns while the other climbs the 40ft wall and starts overrunning characters. Treat each split as its own monster — abilities that target a single monster choose a swarm.

Death. It shrinks as its health drops. When it dies, the last worms wriggle to the ground, leaving a single human skull stained black. Held to an ear, it murmurs faintly.

system.description: +12 to-hit against PD. Deal 2D10+4 Piercing on a hit. 5ft range. You may use this on a creature you have swallowed.
As long as you maintain Focus, wherever you move you leave a trail of ooze. The trail remains for as long as combat continues and is difficult terrain.

This creature may split into multiple parts and merge back together, up to twice. Each split replaces its token with two swarm tokens, each one square smaller than the summed mass, splits its current HP evenly between them, and both keep every level of every condition it had. Every dice type a swarm deals drops by two dice types, and each swarm has 1 less AP.

As an action, a swarm can merge with another of the same size into a larger swarm, reversing all splitting effects (keeping the maximum set of conditions from either swarm). Use the "Csenorras Swarm" actors for the split forms.

Choose one target within 5ft. That target makes Finesse Checks against 5 levels of Pin. If they take at least 1, move over that target's square (centering on it). For as long as that creature has any levels of Pin, they cannot sense anything outside of Csenorras or take reactions, and they take 3D10 Piercing Damage at the start of each of their turns.

Only usable while at least 3×3 in size, and only once per unique target. (Attempts one level less Pin once Csenorras has split.)
This creature is immune to all Physical Adversarial Conditions as well as Prone, Blinded, and Surrounded. It may not be rended.
Rolls Finesse Checks with 1X Advantage.

For as long as that creature has any levels of Pin, they cannot sense anything outside of Csenorras or take reactions, and they take 2D6 Piercing Damage at the start of each of their turns.

Only usable while at least 3×3 in size, and only once per unique target. (Attempts one level less Pin once Csenorras has split.)
This creature is immune to all Physical Adversarial Conditions as well as Prone, Blinded, and Surrounded. It may not be rended.
Rolls Finesse Checks with 1X Advantage.

system.biography:
Level 8 Demon · Medium · Prof. +4 · 4 AP · Talents: Perception +8, Religion +10.

The most intelligent, cunning and dangerous of these demons; her strategy targets the most powerful characters.

Behavior. She won't breach the wall. She summons four Weaverspools: half go after the characters and the ballista, half make for the door and unlock it (an action), letting her wander in.

Her true form. She first appears as an old, frail woman, so the Weaverspools look like the real threat. Below half HP she reveals her sewn-together maw, row after row of rending teeth. If she nears the end of the map and thinks she has won, she takes the form of one of the characters with Change Shape, ready to walk into the town beyond.

Death. She crumples into a pile of magic yarn in shades of blood red, black ichor and yellow bile.

+9 to-hit against MD. Deal 2D10 Force damage on a hit (Mental damage in v1.2 terms). 30ft range.

The Weaver's Daughter may summon 4 Weaverspools in total. They appear in squares adjacent to her. (Drag Weaverspool tokens from the Actors directory; each is its own unlinked creature.)
As long as you maintain Focus, increase the damage of the Bite attack of all Weaverspools within 60ft of you by 1 dice type. Additionally increase their to-hit by +2 and their Check DC by 1.

Level 2 Demon · Small · Prof. +2 · 3 AP · Move 30ft, Climb 30ft · Talents: Perception +8, Acrobatics +8, Nimble Hands +8, Stealth +8.

The Weaver's Daughter's needle-fingered familiars. The Weaver's Daughter summons four of them in total.

Once a target has broken all Pin, this cannot be used against them again.
+5 to-hit against PD. If you hit, the target gains one level of Pin (in addition to Pin they already have been given through Needlepoint) to a maximum of 4. You may only use this once per turn.

Chuni's Wall: a fortified stone wall about 40ft tall. This actor only anchors the scene's Wall Top Region: friendly creatures standing on the walkway or the ballista tower have Height (1X advantage on attacks against creatures below). Its hidden token sits in the east gatehouse; leave it there.

A small piece of heavy paper, upon which a detailed Tianqi glyph emblazons the word "Protection". It is written in blood.

text.content:
Chuni's Wall is a pale and desolate place. Your station here is an isolated and cold one, as you watch northward into the Upper Heibrim. Demons prowl the lands north of here. You have seen them in the night. They wander aimlessly, forever hungering for the flesh of humanity — hungry for you. It is a quiet and tense post. Until it isn't.

A one-shot by Connor Brashar for four level-5 characters, converted to Sacadia's Art of War v1.2.

A short combat event

The players are Tianqi wall guards: soldiers stationed on Chuni's Wall and trained to fight the demons that prowl the Upper Heibrim. A demon tries to breach the gate, and they have to stop it.

The fight has two acts:

  • The Siege. The demon attacks the wall. The characters have the height advantage and the wall's defenses: ballistas, oil barrels, a pit trap. The demon wants into the wall; the players want to defend it and raise the alarm along it.
  • The Breach. Sooner or later the demon gets through and starts to wreak havoc. Now the players must kill it before it goes on to the towns of the Lower Heibrim.

A simplified encounter. The full one-shot pits the party against one of four demons chosen at random (@UUID[RollTable.ab50152d4cf03540]{Which Demon Attacks?}). The introductory version always uses @UUID[Actor.a6332ff14e65fcec]{Wanabbul the Vast}. He isn't the easiest of combatants, but the way he fights shows off dynamics unique to Sacadia. The other demons are on the @UUID[JournalEntry.aee4303672726b2d.JournalEntryPage.ec640ba9f39c3814]{Optional Demons} page.

A combat adventure. This is explicitly a fight. Give your table a little narrative backdrop if they want time to settle into their characters (@UUID[JournalEntry.aee4303672726b2d.JournalEntryPage.dfc8bde2927d57a6]{Background}). If they're here for the fight, don't worry about it.

Combat pacing. Wanabbul could easily down a character by focusing on one of them. In the introductory encounter, spread his attention so nobody feels the fight is hopeless.

What's in this adventure

Scene@UUID[Scene.fcdf52084258c793]{Chuni's Wall}: the battle map (20 × 48 squares) as a two-level scene (the Ground and the Wall Top 40ft up) with walls and line of sight. The defenders are at their starting positions, Wanabbul is to the north, the siege engines are in place, and every feature has a map pin. A Breach Chuni's Wall macro opens the hole when the demon breaks through.
Heroes@UUID[Actor.e873d60291c488cd]{Selthimor}, @UUID[Actor.2c4587b504c27fff]{Chunrudar}, @UUID[Actor.96cb2d186f6fa5a6]{Honnasusara} and @UUID[Actor.d5826497e019d8c5]{Manchuthara}: level-5 Tianqi wall guards, rebuilt as rules-legal v1.2 characters.
DemonsWanabbul the Vast, plus Grubnut, Csenorras the Manyworm (with its split swarms), the Weaver's Daughter and her Weaverspools.
Siege engines & hazardsThe Wall Ballista, the Fixed Ballista and the Oil Barrels (owned by every player, so anyone can crew them), the Pit Trap, and Chuni's Wall.
Handouts@UUID[JournalEntry.f2621eca2654ea7c]{The Breach — Player Handouts}: the characters, how to play each one, Demonology, and a quick-rules sheet.
ItemsThe Tianqi culture's cultural talent, cultural abilities and the Red Glyph of Armor, for players who bring their own Tianqi characters.

Setting up

  1. Open Chuni's Wall and activate it. It has two levels, Ground and Wall Top; @UUID[JournalEntry.aee4303672726b2d.JournalEntryPage.bd4ecf98249930fa]{The Battlefield} explains how they work.
  2. Give each player one of the four heroes: right-click the actor → Ownership → Owner. Everyone can already view every hero (and the handouts), so let them pick first.
  3. Share the @UUID[JournalEntry.f2621eca2654ea7c]{The Breach — Player Handouts} pages: The Characters, then each player's How to Play page.
  4. The fight is already set up in the Combat Tracker, in the one-shot's turn order (the four heroes, then Wanabbul). To roll initiative instead, see @UUID[JournalEntry.aee4303672726b2d.JournalEntryPage.ed7d175ebd8f757f]{Running the Encounter}. When the players are ready, press Begin Combat. For extra drama, open the Combat Tracker's settings (the cog at the top of the tracker) and choose one of Foundry's Combat Themes for sounds at the start of combat and each turn.
  5. Read the Demonology handout aloud as soon as Wanabbul enters the fight.

If a hero dies, that player takes the next unused character. With four players, roll up a fifth Tianqi wall guard or let them crew the siege engines until the end of the fight.

Players bringing their own characters must be level 5. The adventure's Items folder has the Tianqi culture's cultural abilities and inheritance (rulebook v1.2 pp.59–65).

The rules changes from the 2024 PDF are listed on @UUID[JournalEntry.aee4303672726b2d.JournalEntryPage.6463519edb9ae9a6]{Conversion Notes}.

The Tianqi

Highly superstitious and grim, the Tianqi live difficult lives at the edge of humanity. They are deeply religious and wary of magic, yet their culture is bound up with the magic woven through their land. They believe in good against evil, and in their patriotism they are certain they are on the side of good.

Their culture is struggling under the weight of constant demon incursions. These take so much of their military strength that their other neighbors nip at their borders unchallenged. They are tired.

The Tianqi are one of the rulebook's starter cultures (v1.2 pp.59–65): Binding Laws and Customs, the Heibrim Lore cultural talent, and cultural abilities and inheritance. The pregens follow them, and those abilities are in this adventure's Items folder.

The demons

Two hundred years ago, the Tianqi besieged their northern neighbors in the city of Qianpo, meaning to starve them out. The war between the two was so bitter that the Qianpo would not surrender even as they starved. They turned to cannibalism instead. The gods cursed them for it, and everyone who had eaten human flesh became a wild demon.

The Qianpo demons flooded across the land. In a panic, the Tianqi built Chuni's Wall, a vast wall separating the Upper and Lower Heibrim. North of it lie the city of Qianpo and its remaining demons; south of it lies the empire of the Tianqi.

The rulebook adds that the demons of Qianpo are technically Folk Fae, not demons. Tianqi demon lore works on them all the same (Heibrim Lore). This adventure keeps them typed as Demons, as the one-shot does, so a Sentinel's Favored Enemy: Demons applies.

Chuni's Wall

Chuni's Wall is named for the general who proposed and built it. It is a fortified stone wall about 40ft tall, running between the Lake of Western Lights and the Lake of the Jiangshi. Military forts dot it at regular intervals and signal one another with smoke when there's an attack. The wall's guards make up most of Tianqi military strength, and they are trained to fight demons.

The characters

The players take on the roles of the wall guards described on the @UUID[JournalEntry.f2621eca2654ea7c.JournalEntryPage.4c5895fcc37cbbc9]{The Characters} handout. The combat can be very challenging, so if a character dies, that player takes the next unused character.

Starting positions and turn order

The heroes start at assigned positions on the map, set by their role. The scene places them there already. You can ignore the assignments, but they streamline the start and make sure everyone has something to do. The default turn order goes from #1 (first) to #4 (last):

  1. @UUID[Actor.e873d60291c488cd]{Selthimor}, Thug — a melee combatant who helps Chunrudar man the ballista in the opening rounds. He runs faster than Chunrudar, so he starts on the north side of the ballista.
  2. @UUID[Actor.2c4587b504c27fff]{Chunrudar}, Fatebound — a melee combatant working the ballista with Selthimor. He's wise to stay back from the edge of the wall, where the demon can reach him.
  3. @UUID[Actor.96cb2d186f6fa5a6]{Honnasusara}, Soldier — melee plus supporting calls to her allies. She can open by pouring oil, then move east to support Manchuthara or north to support Selthimor and Chunrudar. Either way, she should end up closer to her allies after the barrel.
  4. @UUID[Actor.d5826497e019d8c5]{Manchuthara}, Sentinel — the party's ranged combatant. She can stand at the east end of the wall and fire her crossbow every round, even after the wall is breached.

The Combat Tracker already holds this order: the four heroes at initiative 4, 3, 2 and 1, and Wanabbul at 0. The one-shot doesn't place Wanabbul in the order; putting him after the heroes gives them a full round of siege before he moves.

Rolling initiative instead. Foundry only offers an initiative roll to a combatant that has no initiative yet, so with this order in place there's nothing to roll. To roll, open the ⋮ menu at the top of the Combat Tracker, choose Reset Initiative, then press Roll All (or let each player press Initiative on their sheet). Each combatant rolls a Courage or Finesse Check, whichever is better (v1.2 p.233). To reroll one combatant, right-click it and choose Re-roll Initiative.

Height. Everyone on the wall walkway or the ballista tower is inside the scene's Wall Top Region, which gives friendly tokens the Height status. Height grants 1X advantage on attacks, and with 4+ AP it triggers Manchuthara's Crossbow Mastery. The heroes start with it; it comes and goes as tokens step on and off the wall.

Wanabbul the Vast

@UUID[Actor.a6332ff14e65fcec]{Wanabbul the Vast} is a gigantic, demonic figure who looms to the height of the wall's top: a shadowy shape trailing whisps of black smoke. Lit by a flash of fire, he looks almost hollow.

Behavior.

  • Wanabbul moves forward 20ft every round, through any obstacle. He also has 3 AP.
  • When he reaches the wall, he destroys it in a single turn, then attempts to Grab one nearby character if he can.
  • When he's reduced to half health, on his next turn he sprouts more arms and uses Draining Aura.
  • Optional speed-up: below half health, let him move 25ft or 30ft. The fight ends faster and gets slightly easier.

Death. A humanoid skeleton, the last remnant of his once-human form, falls to the ground while the rest of him dissipates into mist.

Act one: the Siege

Wanabbul starts at the top of the map, about 50ft north of the wall: two or three rounds of approach. Meanwhile:

  • Read the Demonology handout to the players the moment Wanabbul enters the fight.
  • The Wall Ballista begins loaded. Aim, fire, reload: each step costs the crew member 1 AP and both arms. Everything about the siege engines is on @UUID[JournalEntry.aee4303672726b2d.JournalEntryPage.bd4ecf98249930fa]{The Battlefield}.
  • Oil poured on Wanabbul and lit with a torch deals 6D10 Fire.
  • Manchuthara shoots every round. Honnasusara's Standard Bearer (a Boost to her first action of the combat) can Taunt him.

Act two: the Breach

Wanabbul tears through the wall in a single turn, leaving a wide hole that stops anyone crossing east or west along the wall top. Select his token and run the Breach Chuni's Wall macro to open the hole on the map. Point this out to your players as soon as it happens:

  • Two characters on the western wall can jump down onto the tents below without taking damage (they land Prone). A third would be stuck on the wall, or would have to jump onto Wanabbul.
  • The hay bales on the east side work the same way. Each tent and hay pile breaks after one use.
  • Characters can climb Wanabbul: he is gigantic and counts as a slow-moving creature (Power Check at 1X disadvantage, following the climb rules). Movement on him is difficult terrain.
  • Once he's through, his path south runs past the Fixed Ballista and into the Pit Trap on the road.

Grabbed! A character in Wanabbul's hand who loses all their Pin can cling to him (DC 15 Finesse Check) or drop to the ground (6D6 damage). His Drop Boost lets him let go of them as part of another action; they can react with the same DC 15 Finesse Check to cling on.

Fall damage. The one-shot's 6D6 for a fall from Wanabbul's grip is gentler than the rulebook's general rule (v1.2 p.245: a 40ft fall is 16D6 for a Medium creature). It's deliberate, so keep it. Full falls from the wall top use the book rule unless the faller lands in hay or a tent.

Pacing notes

  • Spread Wanabbul's attacks around. Bite plus Punch against a single character can take down Chunrudar or Selthimor in two rounds.
  • The heroes deal roughly 80–100 damage a round once everyone is in reach. With the ballistas and oil, Wanabbul's 600 HP usually lasts six to eight rounds.
  • Healing is scarce. Honnasusara's Call of Healing and the heroes' Healing Dates (each removes one Battle Fatigue) are what they have. A character below 0 HP is Wounded and gains Battle Fatigue each turn. They die at negative half their maximum HP. (These v1.2 rules replace the one-shot's dying counters.)

The defenders are up against a demon much more powerful than they are. To even the odds, the wall gives them several environmental aids. The numbers match the map pins on @UUID[Scene.fcdf52084258c793]{Chuni's Wall}.

The map: two levels

@UUID[Scene.fcdf52084258c793]{Chuni's Wall} uses Foundry's Scene Levels. The level list at the top left of the canvas switches between them:

  • Wall Top (40ft up): the walkway, the ballista tower and the gatehouse. The defenders start here at elevation 40. The parapets stop movement but not sight, so anyone on the wall top sees the whole battlefield. Standing on the walkway or the tower gives a defender Height.
  • Ground: everything else. The wall, the tower and the gatehouse are solid stone here, so nobody on the ground can see or walk through them. Tents block sight and movement; the fences and the palisade stakes block only movement.

Each level sees the other, so the GM's view looks the same on either. What changes is which walls apply and where new tokens go: drag demons in while viewing the Ground level (a dropped token lands on the level you're viewing).

Night. The fight happens at night (Darkness 0.9). Dim moonlight lets everyone see within line of sight. The Tianqi glyphs glow blue along the wall's north face, torches burn on the wall top, and lanterns hang in the camp. Mist lies over the Upper Heibrim north of the wall; the wall holds it back (a Suppress Weather Region over everything south of it). Wanabbul trails a haze of black smoke. The first time he steps forward out of the mist, everyone sees "A shape looms out of the mist…". To brighten the scene, lower the Darkness slider in the scene's lighting settings or from the Lighting controls.

Line of sight. Token Vision is on: each player sees what their hero sees, and you see everything. From the wall top, the defenders see down over the wall they stand on and over the tents, though not something tucked right behind a tent. A hero who climbs down loses sight of everything north of the wall, and of the defenders still on top of it. To share the whole map instead, turn off Token Vision in the scene's settings.

Getting down.

  • The stairs (east, beside the hay) connect the levels. Walk down them on the Wall Top, and at the foot Foundry asks whether to move down to the Ground. To go up, walk onto the foot of the stairs from the camp. They're a solid block on the Ground, so the foot is the only way on or off.
  • Jumping into the hay or onto the tents: set the token's movement to Jump (token HUD) and move off the wall over the hay or the west tents. Foundry asks whether to drop to the Ground. The jumper lands Prone but unharmed; each pile or tent works once.
  • Anyone else stepping off the wall falls 40ft. Move them to the Ground level yourself (token configuration, or drag with the Ground level viewed) and apply the fall.

The front gate is the locked door across the passage where the road meets the wall. When the Weaver's Daughter's Weaverspools get it open, right-click its door icon to unlock it, then click to open it.

The breach. When the demon tears through the wall, select its token and run the Breach Chuni's Wall macro (Macros directory, The Breach folder). It opens a hole in the wall as wide as the token: the wall's faces there come out on the Ground level, the gate goes with them if the hole crosses it, and on the Wall Top the walkway is fenced off at both edges of the hole. From then on no one can cross the wall top east to west. The macro can't be undone; re-importing the adventure restores the scene (and everything else in it).

Crewing a siege engine. The Wall Ballista, the Fixed Ballista and the Oil Barrels are actors every player owns. Select the engine's token (or open its sheet) and use its ability. The engine itself spends nothing: the crew member pays 1 AP and both arms per step, from their own sheet. Like any action, it costs 2 AP if those limbs are already exhausted. The engines' to-hit is their own (1D20+8), not the crew member's.

1 · Wall Ballista

The great ballista on the tower.

  • Aim it: 1 AP. It must be re-aimed every time its target moves, or it automatically misses.
  • Fire it: 1 AP. 150ft range, to-hit 1D20+8 against PD, 8D10 Piercing on a hit.
  • Reload it: 1 AP.
  • It can only be fired at targets north of the wall; it can't be aimed south of the front gate.
  • If a demon deals damage to it, it breaks. It has 1 HP, so any damage applied to its token breaks it.
  • It begins the one-shot loaded.

2 · Oil Barrels

Three tokens: two on the wall walkway and one by the picnic table. Pour a barrel down onto a creature below the wall, or onto the ground (Pour Oil). If an oil-soaked creature is then set alight with a torch, it immediately takes 6D10 Fire Damage: target it and use the barrel's Ignite, which hits automatically. Three of the heroes carry three torches each.

Spilled oil that burns follows the rulebook's Fire in Combat rules (p.246) if you want the fire to spread.

3 · Hay and Tents

Characters can jump from the wall straight into the hay bales (east, beside the stairs) or onto the tents (west) without taking damage, though they land Prone. Each item can be used only once, then it's destroyed.

4 · Fixed Ballista

The wagon-mounted ballista south of the wall follows the same rules as the Wall Ballista, but:

  • it can't be aimed: it only points at the pit trap;
  • it can only be fired once;
  • it deals 12D10 Piercing, to-hit 1D20+8;
  • it breaks if it takes damage from an enemy;
  • it begins the one-shot loaded.

5 · Pit Trap

A demon that makes it this far falls into the pit on the road (the grate on the map), taking 3D10 damage. It then makes Finesse Checks against 5 levels of Pin (if it can take Pin); Check DC 18 negates.

This one is automated. Two Regions over the grate spring it when a hostile token enters: one deals the 3D10, the other posts the Finesse Check card against the @UUID[Actor.0233a1711f2cffda]{Pit Trap}'s Check DC 18. Wanabbul is gigantic, so his checks against Pin get 3X advantage from his size. After the trap springs, open the two Pit Trap Regions and disable their behaviors so it doesn't fire again.

6 · Demonology

The moment Wanabbul enters the fight, the players learn three facts about him. They're on the Demonology handout (@UUID[JournalEntry.f2621eca2654ea7c.JournalEntryPage.15c11401cdf499ae]{Demonology: Wanabbul the Vast}):

  • PD: Wanabbul has 19 PD, and 3 of it can be rended.
  • Bite: he can bite creatures within 5ft, rolling 1D20+12 against their PD, for 2D10+5 damage.
  • Gigantic: he can be climbed. Climbing him takes a Power Check at 1X disadvantage, following the climb rules.

Every hero has Heibrim Lore (Religion: Demon Lore 1). A player who wants more can roll it, and Manchuthara can use Favored Enemy (a Wiles Check against his Check DC) to learn his to-hit, his Trait Expertise, or one of his abilities. A player with the Tianqi Demon Points ability adds +1 damage against Wanabbul for each fact learned this way.

Here are the other demons this module can throw at the wall, each more difficult than the last. The pregens are balanced around Wanabbul, so these are extra challenges. Roll @UUID[RollTable.ab50152d4cf03540]{Which Demon Attacks?} for the one-shot's random demon, or pick one.

To swap demons, delete Wanabbul's token from the scene and drag the new demon onto the top of the map. Their tokens are already sized: Grubnut 3×3, Csenorras 4×4. Read the Demonology handout's facts for the new demon instead (its PD and rendable armor, its signature attack, and its size).

Grubnut

@UUID[Actor.fb3bb6710c64cbd1]{Grubnut} is a writhing, pustulous worm creature. He's less physically intimidating than Wanabbul, but faster: a 20ft move plus Slam's 15ft carries him 35ft a turn.

Behavior. Unlike Wanabbul, Grubnut has no single focus. Above half health he won't move past the characters, and anyone standing in front of him gets his attention. Only below half HP does he race for the edge of the map.

Grubnut and the wall. He can't breach the wall instantly. On his first turn attacking it, the wall splinters; on the second it shatters; on the third he moves through. A Slam into the wall deals 5D10 to it and knocks Prone everyone within 30ft of the impact along the wall who fails a Finesse Check.

Optional map change. He moves much faster than Wanabbul. To make the fight easier, replace the oil barrel by the picnic table with a barrel of grease: knocked over, it creates a 20×20ft square of difficult terrain that slows him for a turn or two.

Death. He begins melting, leaving a strong stench, a sizzling corpse of boils and green ooze, and the outline of a dangerously warped human skeleton.

In the system: his two Pustule options are two abilities (Pustule (Fumes) asks which condition to give; Pustule (Bile) gives Hemorrhage). Use one per Pustule action. Squirming Beast makes him immune to Fatigue and Prone. For Slam, the 1X disadvantage on the Finesse Check is yours to apply.

Csenorras the Manyworm

@UUID[Actor.70ab9b88805de1f5]{Csenorras the Manyworm} is a giant writhing mass of black worms, loosely organized around a human skull somewhere deep within. It keeps a semblance of collective intelligence, but it is alien now.

Behavior. Csenorras is unpredictable and dangerous. In general it moves forward each turn, but once split, only one writhing mass presses forward; the others target individual characters to slow the party down. At the wall it splits in two: one part breaks the wall down over the next two turns while the other climbs the 40ft wall and immediately starts overrunning characters.

Splitting and merging. When it splits, both halves keep every condition the players gave it; when it merges, it keeps the maximum set of conditions from either swarm. Treat the halves as two monsters: a player with an ability that targets a single monster chooses which swarm it hits.

In the system: Csenorras's tokens are unlinked, so each swarm keeps its own HP and conditions. To split it:

  1. Note its current HP and conditions, then delete its token.
  2. Drag in two @UUID[Actor.878f1030f17d02d6]{Csenorras Swarm (split once)} tokens (3×3, 4 AP, dice two types lower).
  3. Set each one's HP to half of what Csenorras had, and copy its conditions onto both.
  4. For a second split, do the same with @UUID[Actor.045deef51b72641a]{Csenorras Swarm (split twice)} (2×2, 3 AP). Those are too small to Swallow.

Swarm Beast makes it immune to the physical adversarial conditions, Prone and Blinded. Surrounded doesn't apply to it, and it can't be rended (its stat block's "PD 20(3)" is overruled by Swarm Beast).

Death. It shrinks as its health drops. When it dies, the last black worms wriggle weakly to the ground, leaving a single human skull stained black with ooze. Held to an ear, it murmurs faintly.

The Weaver's Daughter

@UUID[Actor.e7c4e9fcdf7e59d1]{The Weaver's Daughter} is the most intelligent, cunning and dangerous demon in this module. Her strategy targets the most powerful characters.

Behavior. She won't breach the wall. Instead she summons four @UUID[Actor.bec3b0195c0879b2]{Weaverspools}. Half of them go after the characters and try to sabotage the ballista; the other half make for the door and unlock it with an action, letting her wander in.

Her true form. She conceals it, appearing first as an old, frail woman so the players think the Weaverspools are the real threat. Below half HP she reveals her sewn-together maw, row after row of rending teeth (Rending Bite only works below half health). If she gets near the end of the map and thinks she has won, she takes the form of one of the characters with Change Shape and prepares to walk into the town beyond.

Death. She crumples into a pile of magic yarn in shades of blood red, black ichor and yellow bile.

In the system: Weaverspools are unlinked. Drag up to four onto squares next to her when she summons them. While she maintains Bolster Swarm, Weaverspools within 60ft get +2 to-hit, +1 Check DC and one more die type on Bite. Add those by hand, or with a temporary Active Effect.

The Breach was written in 2024 against an early version of the rules. This adventure updates it to Sacadia's Art of War v1.2. Here is everything that changed, so you can put back anything you prefer.

The heroes

The one-shot's character sheets were hand-simplified: abilities rewritten in plain terms, bespoke pools ("6 Call Points", "6 Trick Strike Points") and some abilities a level-5 character couldn't have. The pregens here are rules-legal level-5 characters built from the system's compendiums, so every ability on their sheets is the real one and the system automates it:

  • level 5: Proficiency +3, 3 AP, 34 Combat Skill Points, 6 Trait Points (no Trait above 2), 10 Talent Points;
  • Tianqi culture: the Heibrim Lore cultural talent (Religion: Demon Lore 1) and the Binding Laws in each hero's Story (Character tab);
  • their level features: Level 3 boon, Rousing Success with 1 Lore Point, and a Level 5 Mastery;
  • HP from the book: profession HP × 5 plus Heritage HP.

Call of Healing is 2D4 temp HP (was 2D6); Courageous Command adds her Courage (+2).

Drunken Fisticuff (re-roll a miss) and Lightning Shove take its place. Fatigue Resilience doesn't exist in v1.2. As a Mist Sylnfolk he resists Water damage by 3.

Targeted Foe adds +1 (half Fate), Imbued Fury attacks AD (the lowest defense), Resilient Foe resists 3, and Crushing Blow adds a die type on a crit. Lucky Break gives 1D6 Fumble to up to 3 enemies within 30ft (Longing Fates).

The heroes' Check DCs are 15 (the one-shot said 14), from the v1.2 formula 9 + profession Trait + Proficiency + Courage/2.

Rules updates

  • Dying. The one-shot's "3 dying levels, roll 1D20+Prof" is the old rule. In v1.2, a creature below 0 HP is Wounded and gains Battle Fatigue each turn, falling unconscious when that takes its AP to 0. It dies at negative half its maximum HP (p.230). The system runs this.
  • Quick rules. The one-shot's quick-reference page is replaced by the v1.2 sheet in the player handouts. Notably, Dodge now needs Medium Armor and a Steadied reaction, and only works against ranged attacks (1D6 at level 5).
  • Healing Dates. The rulebook prints two versions. This adventure uses the First Aid one (p.203): remove one Battle Fatigue, once per target per quick rest.
  • Fall damage. Wanabbul's Grab and Drop keep the one-shot's 6D6. The book's general rule (p.245) would be 16D6 for 40ft. Change it if you want a deadlier drop.
  • Size. The demons' "3X advantage against physical conditions" is the v1.2 size rule (p.224): Gigantic is three sizes above Medium. The system applies it automatically, so it isn't added twice. Grubnut's "1X" becomes the 2X a Huge creature gets.

The demons

Monsters aren't built from player rules, so the stat blocks keep their numbers, with these conversions:

  • NPC stats hold the stat block's full Trait Check modifiers (NPCs have no Proficiency in the system). Each attack's printed to-hit is reached with a bonus scoped to that attack. "Roll with NX Advantage" is a Trait Expertise passive.
  • Defenses. The one-shot gives PD and MD only. TD is set equal to PD (it was one "physical defense" then), and AD to the lowest defense, which is what Chunrudar's Imbued Fury targets.
  • Rend. "PD 19(3)" is a Demonic Hide armor item with 3 PD; rend comes off it. Csenorras can't be rended (Swarm Beast).
  • Damage types. The Weaver's Daughter's Force damage is Mental damage in v1.2.
  • Speed. NPCs now have a Move Speed field: Wanabbul 20ft, Grubnut 20ft (35ft with Slam), Weaverspools 30ft.
  • Grubnut's Pustule is two abilities, one per check: Courage against Delirium or Nausea, or Finesse against Hemorrhage.
  • Csenorras's split forms are actors of their own, with dice two types lower on the v1.2 dice ladder.

Siege engines

The one-shot's player aides are now actors and Regions (see @UUID[JournalEntry.aee4303672726b2d.JournalEntryPage.bd4ecf98249930fa]{The Battlefield}): the ballistas and oil barrels are player-owned actors with their own to-hit, the pit trap is two automated Regions, and the wall walkway is a Region that gives defenders Height.

Chuni's Wall is a pale and desolate place. Your station here is an isolated and cold one, as you watch northward into the Upper Heibrim. Demons prowl the lands north of here. You have seen them in the night. They wander aimlessly, forever hungering for the flesh of humanity — hungry for you. It is a quiet and tense post. Until it isn't.

You are Tianqi wall guards: a stationed group of soldiers trained to fight the demons that prowl the Upper Heibrim. Two hundred years ago the gods cursed the cannibal city of Qianpo, and its people became demons; Chuni's Wall, 40ft of fortified stone, has held them north of the Lower Heibrim ever since. Tonight, one of them comes for the gate.

Pick one of the four heroes below. If yours falls, take the next unused one. Every hero is a level-5 Tianqi, bound by the Tianqi laws and customs in the Story on their sheet's Character tab, and knows the demons through Heibrim Lore (Religion: Demon Lore).

Honnasusara the Soldier

An honored soldier who has manned Chuni's Wall since she was a youth. Honnasusara is human. She wears a breastplate emblazoned with the sigil of the Tianqi, a red and white flower over a blue painted background, and a proud glyphic sigil of protection sticks out from behind her armor: a protective totem for her and her warriors. Tank and support. @UUID[Actor.96cb2d186f6fa5a6]{Honnasusara} · @UUID[JournalEntry.f2621eca2654ea7c.JournalEntryPage.a738b94bff33526c]{How to Play Honnasusara}

Manchuthara the Sentinel

An accomplished warrior and the younger daughter of Honnasusara; a crossbowman and expert marksman. Manchuthara is human. She wears brown trousers tied at the waist and a straw cloak, and has long brown hair and deep brown eyes. Ranged damage. @UUID[Actor.d5826497e019d8c5]{Manchuthara} · @UUID[JournalEntry.f2621eca2654ea7c.JournalEntryPage.7ed0900ace9d6bce]{How to Play Manchuthara}

Selthimor the Thug

Newer to the group, from Tian Chun, a religious capital of the Tianqi. His job is to man the great ballista on top of the wall. Selthimor is a Mist Sylnfolk, with pale grey-blue eyes and hair and pale, off-white skin. He wears white trousers and a white shirt, and doesn't wear a cloak. Melee damage. @UUID[Actor.e873d60291c488cd]{Selthimor} · @UUID[JournalEntry.f2621eca2654ea7c.JournalEntryPage.007aede6104a345b]{How to Play Selthimor}

Chunrudar the Fatebound

Chunrudar is intricately tied to this land: he made a pact with a demon of the mists for power. He wields it as a misty sword and by manipulating fate, fumbling his enemies. He wears blue, flowering robes and has short black hair. His eyes are a misty blue, though they were earthy brown before his recent pact. Melee damage and debuffs. @UUID[Actor.2c4587b504c27fff]{Chunrudar} · @UUID[JournalEntry.f2621eca2654ea7c.JournalEntryPage.830521656176798f]{How to Play Chunrudar}

Bringing your own character

You're welcome to bring your own character instead. Make them level 5. If they're Tianqi, the adventure's Items folder has the culture's cultural talent, cultural abilities and inheritance.

Soldier 5 · Human (Talented) · HP 65 · PD 24 · Move 25ft · Check DC 15

Honnasusara is a frontline ally and a tank. Stay as close to your allies as you can, especially after the wall is breached and everyone closes in on the demon: being near them puts them in range of your calls and reactions.

Your attacks are the weakest in the party, so let support come first.

AttackTo-hitDamage
Spear (5ft, vs TD; can be thrown 40ft)+61D6+3 Piercing
Armored Buckler Bash (5ft, vs PD)+51D8+2 Bludgeoning

Your calls (6 Call Points, back after a quick rest)

Each call is an action that spends one Call Point.

  • Call of Healing: you and every ally within 15ft gain 2D4 temporary HP.
  • Call of Respite: up to two targets within 15ft make Trait Checks against one level of an adversarial condition each (you pick the condition per target).
  • Call of Fury: spend up to 2 extra AP now. One ally within 15ft gets that many extra AP on their next turn. It works especially well on Manchuthara: 4–5 AP crossbow shots are her strongest.

Reactions (one per round)

  • Courageous Command: when an ally within 15ft makes an attack roll, add your Courage (+2) to it. Use it after you see the roll. Selthimor needs to keep hitting, so he benefits greatly.
  • Sacrifice: when an ally within 5ft would take damage from an attack, take it instead.

Drawing the demon's attention

  • Standard Bearer (once, a Boost to your first action of the combat): try to give up to 3 levels of Taunt, split among enemies within 60ft (Courage Checks). Use it to make the demon target you, but be careful: you'll be in grave danger.
  • Imposing Figure (action): try to give one enemy within 10ft 2 Taunt.

Also

  • Stand By Me (Focus): one ally within 5ft adds +1 to all their Trait Checks while you maintain it. Good against Draining Aura and Grab.
  • Rousing Success (1 Lore Point, once): critically succeed at any roll, even after you've rolled.

Your Red Glyph of Armor, written in your own blood, gives +1 MD (already counted). Over a long rest you could move it to PD or TD; edit the effect on the item.

Sentinel 5 · Human (Resilient) · HP 50 · PD 15 · Move 30ft · Check DC 15

Manchuthara is a charged-attack ranged combatant and the party's main source of ranged damage. Most of the time, stand at the east end of the wall and spend your whole turn firing one crossbow shot for maximum damage. You can keep doing that even after the wall is breached.

The charged shot

Your Crossbow (120ft, vs TD) hits at +5, or +7 with Skilled Warrior (once per turn, add your Wiles). Spend extra AP on one shot (a consistent attack) and each extra AP is 1X advantage. With Boltshot and Pullback, each advantage also adds 2D4 damage:

On the wall you have Height, which adds another 1X advantage, and with it another 2D4. Against demons, Favoritism adds +2 damage. At 4 AP or more from the wall, Crossbow Mastery means the shot hits even if it would miss. Ask Honnasusara for her Call of Fury.

Trickshots (6 points, back after a quick rest)

Each Trickshot adds your Wiles (+2) to that attack's to-hit (instead of Skilled Warrior):

  • Head Strike (Boost to a ranged weapon attack): +2D8 damage if you hit. Use it every round.
  • Forceful Strike (action): a ranged attack that deals no damage but pushes the target back 10ft. Use it to slow Wanabbul's advance.

Also

  • Favored Enemy (action): Wiles Check against a demon's Check DC to learn its to-hit, its Trait Expertise, or one of its abilities.
  • Pinning Bolt: on a crossbow critical hit you may give 1 level of Pin.
  • Reactive Mind (reaction): add your Wiles to a Trait Check against a mental condition.
  • Rousing Success (1 Lore Point): critically succeed at any roll, even after you've rolled.

Thug 5 · Fixerfolk (Mist Sylnfolk) · HP 61 · PD 16 · Move 30ft · Check DC 15

Selthimor hits harder every time he hits in a row. Get up to the enemy and punch it as many times as you can. Each consecutive hit against the same target on your turn adds +1 to-hit (Chained Advance) and +1D4 damage (Consecutive Threat), up to +3 / +3D4. A miss ends the chain.

It's crucial to hit often. Standing near Honnasusara (Courageous Command) or surrounding the enemy with your allies makes it easier:

  • Flanking Forces (Boost): when you have a target Surrounded, your first melee attack against it each turn gets 1X advantage.
  • Drunken Fisticuff: once per turn, when you miss with a melee attack, spend 1 more AP to re-roll it. It can save a chain.
  • Pained Bash (action, your head): 3D4+2 damage. Thanks to Tough Skull it doesn't cost you HP, and after four hits in a turn, Bloodthreat adds your Consecutive Threat dice to it too.

Also

  • Natural Wrestler (action, once per turn): try to give a target within 5ft 2 levels of Wrestle Pin (Finesse negates). It's hard against creatures much bigger than you, but useful against the Weaverspools. Kneejerk adds a die type to your melee attacks while your target has exactly 1 Pin.
  • Lightning Shove: 1X advantage on opportunity attacks, and creatures you Kick roll at 1X disadvantage.
  • Semper Steady: your first reaction each turn is always Steadied.
  • Mist-born: as a Sylnfolk of the mists, you resist Water damage by 3.
  • Rousing Success (1 Lore Point): critically succeed at any roll, even after you've rolled.

Fatebound 5 · Human (Craftsman) · HP 55 · PD 16 · Move 30ft · Check DC 15

Chunrudar stabs his enemies with his sword. Play him as an up-close melee fighter once the wall has been breached.

Your greatsword is your divine weapon (Fated Strike adds your Fate to its damage), wreathed in mist by your pact (Elemental Weapon: Rot). You can dismiss or summon it as a Boost to any action, and Rot damage overcomes physical damage resistance.

Targeted Foe (once per combat)

A Focus: choose a target. While you maintain it (1 AP at the start of each of your turns), you get +1 to-hit and damage against it. You also get:

  • Imbued Fury: your attacks against it target its AD, its lowest defense, which greatly increases your chance to hit;
  • Resilient Foe: you resist all damage it deals you by 3;
  • Aware Foe: 1X advantage on Make Trait Check actions against conditions it gives you;
  • Crushing Blow: when you critically hit it, your greatsword's damage goes up one die type.

Be wary: maintaining the Focus costs AP every turn. It's best to wait until the demon has breached the wall and you're in melee range of it.

Lucky Break (once per turn)

An action: up to 3 enemies within 30ft make Fate Checks against your Check DC or take 1D6 Fumble, which reduces their next d20 roll. It's like an extra action when the rest of your turn is Targeted Foe and stabbing, and it's useful early on while you can't reach the demon.

Also

  • Rousing Success (1 Lore Point): critically succeed at any roll, even after you've rolled.

Your GM reads this when the demon enters the fight.

A gigantic shape looms out of the mist, as tall as the wall: a shadowy demon trailing whisps of black smoke. The old tales of the wall name it. Every Tianqi guard has heard of Wanabbul the Vast, and you know three things about him:

  • PD: Wanabbul has 19 PD, and 3 of it can be rended.
  • Bite: he can bite creatures within 5ft, rolling 1D20+12 against their PD. If he hits, he deals 2D10+5 damage.
  • Gigantic: he can be climbed. Climbing him takes a Power Check at 1X disadvantage (he counts as a slow-moving creature). Whatever you roll, rounded down to the nearest 5, is how many feet you can climb along him.

Want to know more? Roll Religion: Demon Lore (your Heibrim Lore), or have Manchuthara use Favored Enemy.

The full rules, and how the system handles each one, are in the @UUID[Compendium.sacadia.user-manual.JournalEntry.521faf57392e4c4b]{Sacadia User Manual}.

Your turn

  • You have 3 AP. Most actions cost 1 AP and exhaust a limb: one arm, both arms, body, mind (your head), focus, or legs. Using a limb that's already exhausted costs +1 AP. The Abilities tab tracks it.
  • Move up to your Move Speed (you can split it). 5ft Adjust is a Boost on a turn you don't Move.
  • Focus abilities cost a Focus action (1 AP) each turn to keep going. You can end a Focus at any time.
  • Help (action): an ally within 5ft gets 1X advantage on one action you name.
  • Climb (action): climb up to 5ft × your Power. Drop (action): drop up to 5ft × your Finesse safely. Drop further, or fall, and you land Prone and take fall damage.
  • Boosts ride on an action (one per action, never on a reaction). Arm a Boost, then take the action.
  • Reactions: one per round, used when it isn't your turn. Steadying (a basic action) makes your reactions stronger.
  • Lore: Rousing Success costs a Lore Point and needs no AP. Use it any time, even after the roll.

On Chuni's Wall

  • The map has two levels: the Wall Top, 40ft up, where you start, and the Ground. From the wall top you see everything; on the ground, the wall blocks your view north.
  • Stairs (east) take you between the levels: walk down them, or onto their foot from the camp, and confirm the level change at the foot.
  • Jump into the hay or onto the tents: set your token's movement to Jump (token HUD), then move off the wall over them. You land Prone but unharmed. Each pile or tent works once.
  • Standing on the walkway or the tower gives you Height: 1X advantage on attacks.

Attacks

  • Roll 1D20 + Proficiency + Trait against the target's defense (PD, TD, MD, or AD, whichever the attack names). AD is a floor under every defense.
  • Frenzied attacks are the regular kind. Consistent attacks spend extra AP on one roll: +1X advantage per extra AP.
  • Advantage rolls extra d20s and keeps the highest. Height, Surrounded and a Prone target give 1X to melee attackers.
  • Critical hit (natural 20): the base damage dice count as their maximum, or another critical effect your abilities offer.
  • Rend Armor (action): a melee attack that deals no damage but rends 1 point of the target's armor.

Basic reactions

  • Block (Steadied): reduce a melee attack against you by 1D6.
  • Dodge (Steadied, Medium Armor): reduce a ranged attack against you by 1D6.
  • Reaction Attack: one melee attack against an enemy leaving your reach.

Trait Checks and conditions

  • A condition is resisted once per level: three levels of Pin means three Finesse Checks against the giver's Check DC. Each failure is one level.
  • At the end of your turn, each adversarial condition drops by one level (unless it's Enduring).
  • Make Trait Check (action): roll against a condition you have to shed levels early.
  • Bigger creatures get advantage against your physical effects: 1X per size step.

Wounded and death

  • Below 0 HP you are Wounded. At the start of each of your turns you gain 1 Battle Fatigue, which lowers your AP. When it would take your AP to 0, you fall Unconscious.
  • Attacks against an Unconscious creature always hit unless the attacker rolls a natural 1.
  • You die at negative half your maximum HP. If you fall, take the next unused hero.
  • A Healing Date removes one Battle Fatigue: an action, a target within 5ft, once per target per quick rest.
